title: WPSB/116/2011 of DR. KALYAN SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 116 of 2011
Dr. Kalyan Singh
 ...Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Others
 ...Respondents
Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State/respondents.
JUDGMENT
 Coram: Honíble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Honíble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Dated: 08th May, 2018
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
 The reliefs sought in the Writ Petition read as
follows:
ì(i) Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing and commanding
the respondents to redetermined the pension of
the petitioner after giving the promoted pay scale
and entire service benefit and the arrears of salary
may be given in accordance with law.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
certiorari quashing the order dated 27.10.2009
and 17.12.2009 passed by the respondent no. 2
and 3 contained in (Annexure No. 5 and 6 to this
writ petition).
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing and commanding the
respondents to refund sum of ` 1,18,763/-, which
has been deducted, by the respondents in
pursuance of the order dated 27.10.2009 and
17.12.2009.î

2
2. Briefly put, the case of the writ petitioner
appears to be as follows:
 The petitioner was appointed as ad-hoc
Medical Officer on 04.5.1977 vide Annexure-1. He
was promoted as Medical Superintendent in the year
1990 on the senior pay scale of Rs. 3000-4050.
Petitioner was posted as Medical Superintendent
from 01.6.1990 to 31.3.1991. Thereafter he was
posted as Assistant Director, Medical
Superintendent, Senior Medical Officer, Medical
Superintendent etc. as stated in paragraph-4 of the
Writ Petition.
 Vide Annexure-3, dated 03.6.2009 the Finance
Controller after 19 years had sent a letter to the
Director General of Medical, Health and Family
Welfare stating therein that the pay scale fixed on
01.01.1990 is by way of mistake and, therefore, the
mistake should be rectified. On 30.4.2009 the
petitioner retired on attaining the age of
superannuation. By Annexure-4 dated 30.4.2009,
the Assistant Accountant sent a letter to the
Director stating therein that on 22.02.1990 when
the promotion was given to the petitioner, the salary
was wrongly determined. By Annexure-5 dated
27.10.2009, the Director General sent a letter to the
Director, Accounts and Pension stating therein that
a sum of ` 1,18,763/- was paid in excess to the
petitioner due to wrong fixation of pay scale, and the
same has to be recovered from gratuity. On
17.12.2009, the Pension Directorate sent a letter to
the Director General stating therein that there is
excess payment of the aforesaid amount and the
same has to be recovered.

3
 No show cause was issued to the petitioner,
and no opportunity of hearing was provided before
recovery, is the complaint of the petitioner. The case
of the petitioner is that the pay scale was fixed in
1990 and the payment has been made till his
retirement, and there is no misrepresentation and
fraud played by the petitioner. Since the amount
was deducted, the amount has to be repaid.
3. Pleadings have been exchanged. We heard Mr.
S.K. Mandal, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.
Pradeep Joshi, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner drew our
attention to the judgment of Honíble Apex Court in the
case of ëState of Punjab and Others Etc. vs. Rafiq
Masih (White Washer) etc. reported in 2015 (1)
Supreme 671. Therein, the Apex Court after considering
the matter, has laid down inter alia among situations,
where recovery would be impermissible, recovery from
retired employees or employees who are due to retire
within one year of the order of recovery, instant case falls
within those exceptions where recovery would be
impermissible.
5. In this case, petitioner retired on 30.4.2009.
The impugned orders are issued after he retired.
Petitioner has a definite case, also that there is no
misrepresentation on his part or fraud. This is also not a
case where recovery is sought to be done based on any
disciplinary proceedings. In such circumstances, the
impugned orders and the recovery made on the strength
of the same cannot be sustained.

4
6. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is partly allowed,
as what is pressed before us is relief nos. 2 & 3, and we
also direct that the amount of ` 1,18,763/-, which has
been deducted, will be refunded by the respondents to
the petitioner at the earliest and at any rate within 6
weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of
this judgment before the respondents.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 08.5.2018
Pooja
